editions.label: Tue 13 Oct · Morning
editions.brief: Qatar Airways suspending flights to Riyadh and Dammam after Houthi attacks on Saudi airports was the main news item, carried by Reuters, US and Israeli outlets. Israeli outlets also led on a report that Netanyahu aide Yonatan Urich used ChatGPT to craft pro-Qatar messaging during the Gaza war, with Naftali Bennett using it to attack the prime minister. US coverage mentioned Qatar mainly within wider Iran, Hormuz and oil market reporting.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways suspends Riyadh, Dammam flights as airport attacks disrupt air travel
stories.summary: Qatar's flag carrier halted service to two Saudi cities after Houthi attacks on Saudi airports disrupted air travel.

stories.headline: Etihad, Qatar Airways suspend flights to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Both Gulf carriers paused flights to Saudi Arabia after the Houthi strikes.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways suspends its flights to Riyadh and Dammam
stories.summary: Live-blog entry reporting the Qatari airline's suspension of two Saudi routes.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways Halts Flights to Saudi Airports Amid Attacks
stories.summary: Qatar Airways stopped flights to Saudi airports as Houthi attacks continued.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways suspend flights to Saudi hubs following Houthi attacks in Riyadh
stories.summary: Live blog notes that Qatar Airways and Etihad suspended flights to Saudi hubs after attacks on Riyadh.

stories.headline: PM's aide Urich used ChatGPT to create pro-Qatar messaging campaign, report says
stories.summary: A report says Netanyahu aide Yonatan Urich used ChatGPT to devise a messaging campaign meant to improve Qatar's image during the Gaza war.

stories.headline: Netanyahu aide asked ChatGPT how to 'whitewash Qatar' during Gaza war, report says
stories.summary: Ynet reports that the aide queried an AI chatbot about improving Qatar's image while the war in Gaza was under way.

stories.headline: Report: Netanyahu aide questioned over alleged use of AI to boost Qatar's image
stories.summary: Haaretz reports police questioned the aide over his alleged use of AI to shape pro-Qatar messaging.

stories.headline: Bennett slams PM for keeping Qatar-linked aides, says he cannot remain in government
stories.summary: Opposition figure Naftali Bennett criticised the prime minister for keeping aides tied to the Qatargate affair.

stories.headline: Shadows in Doha
stories.summary: Blog post on Qatari influence and its ties to Israeli politics.

mentions.headline: Iran Is Fortifying Nuclear Sites and Rallying Its People for a Return to Fighting
mentions.context: References Qatar in coverage of Iran's nuclear program and the prospect of renewed fighting.

mentions.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Weigh Middle East Risks, Russian Diesel Supplies
mentions.context: References Qatar in coverage of oil markets and Middle East risks.

mentions.headline: Houthi rebels say multiple airstrikes targeted them in Yemen, and other Mideast developments
mentions.context: References Qatar in coverage of Houthi attacks and other Mideast developments.

mentions.headline: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
mentions.context: References Qatar in coverage of Houthi attacks on Saudi airports.

mentions.headline: I.M.F. Warns Mideast War Will Widen Gap Between Rich and Poor Countries
mentions.context: References Qatar in coverage of the IMF's warning on the economic impact of the Mideast war.

editions.label: Mon 12 Oct · Morning
editions.brief: Qatar coverage centred on Israeli outlets revisiting the Qatargate affair, with opinion and analysis pieces on alleged Qatari influence in Israel and on Qatar's role as funder and mediator in Gaza. A Reuters column looked at how the Iran conflict still weighs on Gulf LNG exports. US outlets carried little Qatar-specific news, with Iran and Hormuz diplomacy dominating the wider regional picture.

stories.headline: The Blogs: How Doha Bought Its Influence in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Blog post argues Qatar built political and media influence in Israel over the years through money and access.

stories.headline: Exclusive: New Evidence Links Netanyahu Aide Yonatan Urich To Qatar Influence Campaign
stories.summary: An investigation reports new evidence linking a Netanyahu aide to an alleged Qatari influence campaign in Israeli media, as part of the Qatargate affair.

stories.headline: "The arsonist and the firefighter of the Middle East": How Qatar became a lever of influence in Gaza
stories.original_headline: "המציתה והכבאית של המזרח התיכון": כך קטאר הפכה למנוף השפעה בעזה
stories.summary: The piece argues that Qatar used its role as both funder and mediator to build leverage over events in Gaza.

stories.headline: Qatar Stars League: Oussama Tannane scores for Al-Arabi
stories.summary: Al-Arabi forward Oussama Tannane scored in a Qatar Stars League match.

stories.headline: Netanyahu evades responsibility on Qatar and Oct. 7
stories.summary: Opinion piece argues Netanyahu is dodging accountability over Qatari funding and the October 7 attack.

stories.headline: Qatar’s $100M Gaza Aid Exposed
stories.summary: Report examines about $100 million in Qatari aid to Gaza and how it was used.

stories.headline: COMMENTARY: Middle East LNG industry remains hostage of Iran war
stories.summary: The column argues that Gulf gas exporters, Qatar's LNG sector among them, remain constrained by the Iran conflict and the risks around Hormuz.

editions.label: Sun 11 Oct · Evening
editions.brief: Only one tracked outlet story about Qatar could be confirmed in this window. The Jerusalem Post covered a think tank ranking of states most likely to join the Abraham Accords, in which Qatar was assessed as unlikely to normalize soon. No US outlet items were confirmed, so no difference in framing could be drawn.

stories.headline: Kuwait, Lebanon, Syria leading options for Abraham Accords expansion, CSA report assesses
stories.summary: A Council for a Secure America report ranks nine states for possible normalization with Israel and judges Qatar unlikely to join soon because of its ties to Iran and the Muslim Brotherhood.

editions.label: Sun 11 Oct · Morning
editions.brief: Qatar coverage in this window was light. The one qualifying story, from an Israeli outlet, covered the Red Cross president's account of meeting Hamas's Ismail Haniyeh in Qatar to seek access to hostages in Gaza. No US outlets or wires with a confirmed timestamp in this window were found.

stories.headline: Red Cross chief says she tried to arrange Gaza hostage visits through talks with Hamas's Haniyeh
stories.summary: The Red Cross president said in a New York Times interview that she met Ismail Haniyeh twice in Qatar to try to arrange visits to hostages in Gaza, and that the organization still has no access to them.

editions.brief: Our first edition looks back over the past ten days. Gulf security dominated coverage: a tanker hit by projectiles off Qatar's north coast, US Patriot batteries sent to protect Gulf energy sites, and a US senator saying the Pentagon kept him out of Al Udeid. Israeli papers also covered the World Bank's forecast of a 4.3% contraction across Gulf economies this year.
editions.label: Launch · 1–11 Oct

stories.headline: Tanker off Qatar reports hits from multiple projectiles, says maritime agency
stories.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by several projectiles north of Madinat ash Shamal, with casualties reported. Lead item on the Oct. 7 live blog.

stories.headline: Middle East economy to shrink 2.1% in 2026, Gulf economies by 4.3%, World Bank forecasts
stories.summary: World Bank projects the Gulf's deepest contraction in years as the Iran war disrupts energy exports.

stories.headline: RFK Jr. deletes post claiming Israel accusations stem from Qatar-funded Muslim Brotherhood campaign
stories.summary: The HHS secretary removed a social media post blaming criticism of Israel on a Qatar-funded campaign.

stories.headline: US Senator Murphy says Pentagon denied him access to US base in Qatar
stories.summary: Sen. Chris Murphy says the Pentagon refused him a visit to Al Udeid and a war briefing while he was in the region.

stories.headline: US sends Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia, Qatar to protect oil, gas facilities - report
stories.summary: Report says Washington is deploying additional Patriot batteries to shield Gulf energy infrastructure from Iranian strikes.
